policy_set_lamp_said_done: Lamp on, instruction 'off': one press needed. The policy turns in place for 10 s (it never moves more than 4.5 cm) and says done at tick 103, just as the bot's own opening look-around would end (the shadow bot is still in it). It never goes near the plate. This is the policy's most common set-lamp failure: 249 of 301 press-needed test episodes.
policy_set_lamp_floor: Lamp on, instruction 'on': no press needed. The policy looks around, drifts 27 cm and says done at 37.5 s. It scores because the lamp already matched, the same way 'say done at once' would. All 264 of its set-lamp successes are of this kind.
policy_go_and_return_pad: Target yellow, 1.4 m away. The policy walks straight to the yellow pad and is on it at 18 s (the bot's own run on this room: 23 s). Then it stops: for the remaining 100 s it turns slowly on the spot near the pad, 1.6 m from home, and never says done. The way back is the part that needs memory of where home is (the hypothesis in RESULTS M5). (The shadow bot's log says 'home' at 86 s and it stops labelling there; it isn't driving, so its plan and the duck's position have parted.)
policy_find_ball: The ball rolls behind a hider in the first seconds. The policy turns in place for the whole 60 s (it never moves more than 6 cm) and never looks for it. The shadow bot never asked to walk either: in this episode it only asked to turn and look.
bot_set_lamp_appearances: New appearance; lamp off, instruction 'on'. The bot sees the lamp off, walks to the plate and presses at 33 s: the lamp goes on. It then walks to a spot from which to check the lamp, and on the way steps on the plate again at 47 s: the lamp goes off. Its final lamp check at 74 s gets no reading and it says done. Its memory also holds a second 'button' on top of the blue pad (the test button hue sits next to the pad colours, prediction 1).
bot_go_and_return_appearances: New appearance; target blue. The bot doesn't see blue in its opening look-around, explores, and reaches the blue pad at 70 s. Its memory has no mat at all: the test mat's colour is past the bot's mat limit (prediction 2), so it homes on odometry alone. It ends up on the wrong side of a wall-attached partition, walking along it 0.7 m from home (34 ticks of contact) until time runs out.
bot_find_ball_partition: New arrangement; the ball rolls behind a free-standing partition. The bot's guess of where it stopped is within 10 cm of the true spot. But it searches from the near side, never goes round the partition (closest 0.48 m), and at 57.8 s says done without the ball in view. Its memory also holds four 'mat' tracks: two near its home mat, one on the red pad.
